finance.label: Retail banking, payments and lending

stakeholders.wants: to see the true balance and move money without doubt
stakeholders.fears: a transfer that silently failed, or a fee they did not see
stakeholders.designImplication: the balance is the single most-read number in the product. It never animates, never abbreviates, never rounds

stakeholders.wants: the customer's whole position on one screen
stakeholders.fears: advising against a fact they could not see
stakeholders.designImplication: internal screens are dense and tabular by requirement, not by preference

stakeholders.wants: to prove afterwards who did what
stakeholders.fears: an action with no attributable actor
stakeholders.designImplication: every state-changing screen needs a recorded actor and timestamp, and this is a screen, not a log file

stakeholders.wants: to stop a payment mid-flight
stakeholders.fears: a queue with no age on it
stakeholders.designImplication: a pending state must show how long it has been pending

stakeholders.wants: evidence of fair treatment and disclosure
stakeholders.fears: a cost the customer was not shown before consenting
stakeholders.designImplication: fees and rates appear on the confirmation screen, never only in terms

standards: ISO 20022 for payment messaging
ISO 8583 for card authorisation
PCI DSS where card data is touched
Open Banking / PSD2 strong customer authentication in applicable markets
finance.regulator: central bank plus the market conduct authority

colour.leads: deep blue or navy, with a restrained secondary
colour.why: blue is the sector's inherited signal for solvency and permanence. Deviating from it is a positioning decision, not a taste one, and it must be argued

avoid.what: red as a brand or accent colour
avoid.why: red is load-bearing here: it means negative, declined, or overdrawn. Spending it on a button destroys the one signal that must never be ambiguous

avoid.what: neon and high-chroma playful palettes
avoid.why: they read as a promotion, and a custody product cannot afford to read as a promotion

avoid.what: green for anything other than settled or in credit
avoid.why: same reason as red, in the other direction

style.tradition: international / Swiss typographic style, executed flat with restrained elevation
style.why: the product is a table of numbers and a set of irreversible actions. Grid discipline and typographic hierarchy do the work; ornament competes with the figures

notThis.what: glassmorphism, because translucency reduces the contrast of the one number that must be unambiguous
neubrutalism, because its deliberate crudeness reads as unfinished on a product holding money
skeuomorphism, because the physical metaphors it borrows are the ones the sector left behind

finance.density: high on desktop internal screens, comfortable on customer mobile. Two densities in one product, declared separately
finance.typography: tabular numerals are mandatory wherever an amount appears, so columns of money align on the decimal. Currency symbol and sign never rendered smaller than the figure
finance.tone: precise and unhurried. Never jocular about a failure. 'Your transfer was not sent' beats 'Oops, something went wrong', because the second one does not say whether the money moved
forbidden: animating a balance so it cannot be read immediately
hiding a fee behind a disclosure the user has to open
an irreversible transfer with no confirmation step naming the recipient in full

insurance.label: Insurance: policy, quote and claims

stakeholders.wants: to know whether this thing is covered
stakeholders.fears: discovering an exclusion at the moment of the claim
stakeholders.designImplication: exclusions are never rendered smaller or later than benefits. That asymmetry is the sector's characteristic design failure

stakeholders.wants: to compare and place quickly
stakeholders.fears: quoting a price that will not hold
stakeholders.designImplication: a quote carries its own expiry, visibly

stakeholders.wants: the risk factors that drove the price
stakeholders.fears: a decision they cannot reconstruct
stakeholders.designImplication: a price is shown with its factors, not as a single number

stakeholders.wants: evidence and policy terms side by side
stakeholders.fears: paying outside cover, or refusing inside it
stakeholders.designImplication: the claim screen and the policy screen are one screen

stakeholders.wants: clean structured data out of every form
stakeholders.fears: free text where a code was needed
stakeholders.designImplication: free-text fields are a data decision, and each one needs a reason

standards: ACORD standards for policy and claims data exchange

colour.leads: blue or teal, with a strict semantic triad for cover status: green covered, amber pending, red not covered
colour.why: the product's whole job is to answer covered / pending / not covered, and that answer must be readable before any text is

avoid.what: using the status triad decoratively anywhere else
avoid.why: once green means covered, a green button means covered

avoid.what: colour as the only channel for cover status
avoid.why: an exclusion the user missed because of colour vision is a dispute, and the sector is regulated on disclosure

style.tradition: editorial, document-forward, restrained
style.why: the deliverable genuinely is a document. Designing away from that makes the terms feel optional, and they are not

notThis.what: maximalism, which competes with the small print that is legally load-bearing
anything that renders terms in a scrolling box shorter than four lines

insurance.density: high in policy detail, deliberately low in the claim wizard: a person filing a claim has just had a bad day
insurance.typography: body text minimum 16px. Exclusions set at the same size and weight as benefits, always
insurance.tone: plain language, and in several markets that is a legal requirement rather than a style preference
forbidden: exclusions in smaller type than benefits
a quote with no visible expiry
pre-ticked consent for data sharing

healthcare.label: Clinical and patient-facing healthcare

stakeholders.wants: to understand what happens next
stakeholders.fears: being told something they cannot act on
stakeholders.designImplication: low density, plain language, one action per screen. This is the opposite of the clinician's screen

stakeholders.wants: everything relevant without navigating
stakeholders.fears: a fact that existed and was not shown
stakeholders.designImplication: high density is a clinical safety requirement here, not a preference. Pagination hides facts

stakeholders.wants: to act fast, often standing, often gloved
stakeholders.fears: mis-tapping a dose
stakeholders.designImplication: larger targets than the clinician's desktop screen, and dose entry that cannot be ambiguous

stakeholders.wants: to book and correct records quickly
stakeholders.fears: attaching a record to the wrong person
stakeholders.designImplication: patient identity confirmation is its own step, with more than one identifier

stakeholders.wants: to help without being the patient
stakeholders.fears: not being allowed to see what they need
stakeholders.designImplication: delegated access is a first-class concept, not an afterthought

stakeholders.wants: a defensible retention and access trail
stakeholders.fears: an access with no recorded reason
stakeholders.designImplication: reason-for-access prompts belong in the design, not in policy

standards: HL7 FHIR for records exchange
SNOMED CT for clinical terms
ICD-10 or ICD-11 for diagnosis coding
DICOM where imaging is involved
healthcare.regulator: national health authority plus the professional registration body

colour.leads: calm blues and teals, with red reserved absolutely
colour.why: red means clinical emergency in every hospital in the world. A product that spends it on a delete button has broken a convention older than the product

avoid.what: red and green as the only distinction between two states
avoid.why: colour vision deficiency is roughly one in twelve men, and clinicians are not screened for it

avoid.what: saturated warning colours on routine screens
avoid.why: alarm fatigue is a documented clinical harm, not a metaphor

style.tradition: flat, clinical, high-contrast, near-zero ornament
style.why: every pixel of decoration is a pixel not spent on a value someone will act on

notThis.what: playful or illustrative treatments on clinician screens
low-contrast greys, which fail under the lighting these screens actually run in

healthcare.density: two products in one: high for clinicians, low for patients. Declare them as separate density decisions or one of the two will be wrong
healthcare.typography: tabular numerals for every dose, vital sign and result. Drug names never abbreviated and never truncated with an ellipsis
healthcare.tone: factual, never reassuring about outcome, never diagnostic. The product reports; the clinician decides
forbidden: a dose field that accepts an ambiguous unit
truncating a drug name
any screen that offers a clinical interpretation the product is not registered to give
colour as the only channel for an abnormal result

pharmacy.label: Pharmacy, dispensing and medication management

stakeholders.wants: to catch an interaction before dispensing
stakeholders.fears: dispensing against a look-alike name
stakeholders.designImplication: look-alike drug names are the sector's signature failure. Tall-man lettering is the conventional mitigation and it is a typographic decision

stakeholders.wants: a queue that is unambiguous
stakeholders.fears: picking the wrong strength
stakeholders.designImplication: strength is never rendered as a suffix in the same weight as the name

stakeholders.wants: to know when and how to take it
stakeholders.fears: taking two things that conflict
stakeholders.designImplication: schedule is a picture, not a sentence

stakeholders.wants: to know it was collected
stakeholders.fears: silent non-adherence
stakeholders.designImplication: collection status is a state worth designing

stakeholders.wants: a controlled-drug trail
stakeholders.fears: a dispense with no attributable pharmacist
stakeholders.designImplication: the responsible pharmacist is a required field on the screen, not an inferred session value

standards: HL7 FHIR for prescription exchange
dispensing and controlled-drug record requirements set by the national regulator
pharmacy.regulator: pharmacy council or equivalent registration body

colour.leads: green or teal for health and availability, with amber hard-reserved for interaction and dispensing warnings
colour.why: the sector inherits green from health signage, and the warning channel has to survive being the only thing a rushed reader sees

avoid.what: differentiating strengths by colour alone
avoid.why: 5mg and 50mg differing only in hue is a dispensing error waiting for a tired afternoon

style.tradition: flat and utilitarian, with typographic emphasis doing the safety work
style.why: the safety mechanism in this sector is legibility, and legibility is typography

notThis.what: decorative type on any surface carrying a drug name or strength

pharmacy.density: high at the dispensing counter, low on the patient's schedule view
pharmacy.typography: tall-man lettering for confusable drug names, tabular numerals for strengths, strength always adjacent to the name and never wrapped away from it
pharmacy.tone: instructional and unambiguous. Never soften a warning to be friendly
forbidden: truncating a drug name or strength
colour as the only distinction between strengths
a dispense action with no named responsible pharmacist

education.label: Education and learning, from schools to training

stakeholders.wants: to know what to do next and whether they are getting it
stakeholders.fears: being shown they are behind, in front of others
stakeholders.designImplication: progress is shown against the learner's own past, never ranked against peers by default. And the age band changes the product entirely: a seven-year-old and a seventeen-year-old are not one audience

stakeholders.wants: to see the whole class and act on the outliers
stakeholders.fears: marking work twice, or missing a student who went quiet
stakeholders.designImplication: the teacher's gradebook is dense and tabular. The learner's screen is not. Same product, two densities

stakeholders.wants: to know how their child is doing without decoding jargon
stakeholders.fears: finding out about a problem too late
stakeholders.designImplication: the parent view is a third density, and it must translate rather than expose the teacher's terms

stakeholders.wants: enrolment, attendance and reporting to reconcile
stakeholders.fears: a statutory return that does not tie out
stakeholders.designImplication: attendance and enrolment are audit surfaces, not conveniences

stakeholders.wants: safeguarding and data minimisation for minors
stakeholders.fears: child data leaving the jurisdiction or the purpose
stakeholders.designImplication: consent is parental below the age threshold, and the threshold varies by market

standards: not applicable in most builds: no mandated external exchange. Where interoperability is required, SCORM or xAPI for course content and OneRoster for rostering
education.regulator: education authority, plus the data protection regulator acting on child data

colour.leads: warm and optimistic: a trustworthy blue or green base with a warm accent such as amber or coral
colour.why: the sector's job is to make a person feel safe enough to be wrong in public. Cool corporate palettes read as assessment, and assessment is what learners are already afraid of

avoid.what: red for an incorrect answer, especially for young learners
avoid.why: red marking carries a shame response that is well documented in classroom practice. Use a neutral state plus guidance toward the right answer

avoid.what: corporate grey and navy as the dominant pair
avoid.why: it reads as administration software, and the learner is not an administrator

avoid.what: leaderboards by default
avoid.why: ranking is a motivation decision with known harm to the bottom of the ranking, so it is a decision to argue, not a default

reserved.for: nothing a learner did. It is not spent on wrong answers

style.tradition: friendly geometric with generous rounding and illustration, restrained toward the teacher and admin surfaces
style.why: illustration is expected and effective for learners and actively counterproductive on a gradebook a teacher uses for four hours

notThis.what: business or admin dashboard styling on the learner surface, which is the single most common failure in this sector
dense data-table styling for anyone under about fourteen

education.density: three densities in one product: low for the learner, high for the teacher's gradebook, medium and translated for the parent
education.typography: generous line height and a larger minimum size for younger learners. Dyslexia-considerate choices matter here more than in any other sector: avoid tightly-spaced geometric letterforms where b, d, p and q mirror each other
education.tone: encouraging and specific. 'Not quite, try the second step again' beats both 'Wrong' and 'Great effort!', because only one of the three says what to do
forbidden: ranking learners against each other without an explicit decision to do so
collecting more child data than the stated purpose needs
red-marking a young learner's mistake as the only feedback

legal.label: Legal practice and contract work

stakeholders.wants: the document and its history without losing the thread
stakeholders.fears: acting on a superseded version
stakeholders.designImplication: version is always on screen, never inferred from a filename

stakeholders.wants: to assemble and cross-reference at speed
stakeholders.fears: a citation that does not resolve
stakeholders.designImplication: every reference is a link that can be proven to resolve

stakeholders.wants: to know cost and position in plain words
stakeholders.fears: an invoice they cannot map to work
stakeholders.designImplication: time entries map to a matter and are visible to the client

stakeholders.wants: matter profitability and risk exposure
stakeholders.fears: a conflict of interest discovered late
stakeholders.designImplication: conflict checking is a gate in the flow, not a report

stakeholders.wants: privilege and client confidentiality preserved
stakeholders.fears: privileged material in a shared surface
stakeholders.designImplication: sharing controls are per document, defaulting closed

standards: not applicable: no mandated exchange format in most jurisdictions. Court filing systems impose their own where relevant

colour.leads: deep neutrals with a single restrained accent, often burgundy, navy or forest
colour.why: the sector's visual language is inherited from print and from institutions that advertise longevity. Restraint reads as competence here in a way it does not elsewhere

avoid.what: bright multi-hue palettes
avoid.why: they read as consumer software, and the buyer is buying judgement

colour.reservedNote: no hue is load-bearing in this sector, so the palette is a brand decision rather than an inherited constraint

style.tradition: editorial, typographic, print-derived
style.why: the artefact is a document and the reading experience is the product

notThis.what: card-heavy dashboard styling that fragments a document into tiles

legal.density: high. These are professional users reading long documents for hours, and whitespace that helps a consumer costs them scrolling
legal.typography: a serif or humanist face for document body is conventional and defensible. Line length capped for sustained reading. Clause numbering never reflows
legal.tone: precise and hedged where the law is hedged. The product must never state a legal conclusion
forbidden: presenting output as legal advice
a document view that does not name its version
sharing that defaults open

ecommerce.label: Retail and e-commerce

stakeholders.wants: to find it, trust it, and know the real total
stakeholders.fears: a cost that appears at the last step
stakeholders.designImplication: the full price including shipping and tax appears before the final step. Late-revealed cost is the single largest documented cause of cart abandonment

stakeholders.wants: to control what is seen first
stakeholders.fears: a product surfaced with a bad image
stakeholders.designImplication: image quality is a system constraint, and the design must specify what happens when it is not met

stakeholders.wants: the order and its history in one place
stakeholders.fears: contradicting the tracking page
stakeholders.designImplication: the agent sees exactly the states the customer sees, named identically

stakeholders.wants: unambiguous pick data
stakeholders.fears: a variant that reads the same as another
stakeholders.designImplication: variant naming is a design decision with a physical consequence

stakeholders.wants: honest pricing and a working right to return
stakeholders.fears: a dark pattern in the checkout
stakeholders.designImplication: no pre-ticked add-ons, no countdown that is not real, no obstructed cancellation

standards: not applicable to the storefront: payment is delegated to a provider, which carries PCI DSS. Product data exchange conventionally uses GS1 identifiers

colour.leads: brand-led, with a single high-contrast action colour that appears nowhere else
colour.why: this is the one sector where the palette is genuinely the brand's to choose. What is not negotiable is that the buy action owns a colour exclusively

avoid.what: spending the action colour on secondary controls
avoid.why: if three things are the action colour, none of them is the action

avoid.what: red for urgency banners while also using red for errors
avoid.why: the two collide at exactly the moment the checkout fails

colour.reservedNote: no hue is load-bearing in this sector, so the palette is a brand decision rather than an inherited constraint

style.tradition: editorial for considered purchases, flat and utilitarian for high-frequency ones
style.why: the style follows the purchase cadence: a sofa is browsed, a razor refill is repurchased. They are not the same product

notThis.what: heavy chrome or ornament between the product image and the buy action

ecommerce.density: low on product, high on order history and admin
ecommerce.typography: price is the second most important run on the page after the product name, and it uses tabular numerals wherever prices stack
ecommerce.tone: direct. Say what it costs and when it arrives
forbidden: revealing shipping cost only at the final step
a countdown or stock-scarcity claim that is not true
pre-ticked add-ons or subscriptions
making cancellation harder than signing up

hospitality.label: Food, restaurants and hospitality

stakeholders.wants: to decide quickly and eat
stakeholders.fears: an allergen they were not told about
stakeholders.designImplication: allergen information is never behind a tap. In several markets that is law, not courtesy

stakeholders.wants: to fire an order without going back to a terminal
stakeholders.fears: a modifier that did not reach the kitchen
stakeholders.designImplication: modifiers are confirmed visually at the point of sending, not assumed

stakeholders.wants: the order in preparation sequence
stakeholders.fears: a rush of tickets with no ordering
stakeholders.designImplication: the kitchen display is a different product from the menu, with its own density and its own colour logic

stakeholders.wants: covers, turn time and stock in one view
stakeholders.fears: selling something that ran out an hour ago
stakeholders.designImplication: availability is a live state on the menu, not a nightly update

stakeholders.wants: accurate allergen declaration
stakeholders.fears: an undeclared allergen
stakeholders.designImplication: the allergen field is required, and the design must state what happens when it is unknown

standards: not applicable for exchange. Allergen declaration requirements are set nationally and are binding on the interface
hospitality.regulator: food standards or public health authority

colour.leads: warm appetite colours: reds, oranges, warm neutrals, deep greens for fresh and plant-based
colour.why: warm hues are conventionally associated with appetite and the sector has built on that for a century. Deep green now reads as fresh rather than as institutional

avoid.what: blue as a dominant colour on food imagery surfaces
avoid.why: blue is rare in edible food and reads as spoilage or artificiality against a plate. It is fine in the booking flow and wrong on the menu

avoid.what: colour as the only allergen signal
avoid.why: an allergen notice that a colour-blind guest cannot read is an allergen notice that does not exist

colour.reservedNote: no hue is load-bearing in this sector, so the palette is a brand decision rather than an inherited constraint

style.tradition: editorial and photographic for the menu, flat and utilitarian for the kitchen display
style.why: the menu sells with photography and typography; the kitchen screen is read at three metres in a hurry

notThis.what: low-contrast type over food photography without a scrim, which is the sector's most common legibility failure

hospitality.density: low on the menu, very high on the kitchen display, medium at the point of sale
hospitality.typography: menu type may be expressive. Allergen and price runs may not, and they never sit below 14px
hospitality.tone: appetising for the menu, terse for operations. They are different voices in the same product
forbidden: allergen information behind an extra tap
a price that excludes service charge without saying so
photography that misrepresents portion or preparation

logistics.label: Logistics, freight and last-mile delivery

stakeholders.wants: to scan and move on
stakeholders.fears: a mis-scan they do not notice
stakeholders.designImplication: this user is gloved, standing, in cold or noise, often on a rugged handheld. Control targets go well above the usual minimum and confirmation is haptic or audible, not only visual

stakeholders.wants: the next stop and proof of delivery
stakeholders.fears: an address they cannot find and a clock that is running
stakeholders.designImplication: one-handed, in sunlight, sometimes moving. Maximum contrast, minimum reading

stakeholders.wants: the whole network state and the exceptions
stakeholders.fears: an exception nobody surfaced
stakeholders.designImplication: the exception queue is the primary screen, not a filter on a list

stakeholders.wants: to know when, within an hour
stakeholders.fears: a window so wide it is useless
stakeholders.designImplication: a tracking state with no time attached is not a tracking state

stakeholders.wants: documentation that matches the goods
stakeholders.fears: a consignment with no attributable chain
stakeholders.designImplication: custody handover is an audited event with a named actor at each end

standards: UN/EDIFACT for consignment messaging
GS1 barcode and SSCC identifiers for units and pallets

colour.leads: high-contrast utility palette, usually a strong single brand hue with amber and red reserved for exception states
colour.why: these screens are read in sunlight, in cold stores, and through scratched screen protectors. Contrast is a functional requirement rather than an aesthetic one

avoid.what: subtle greys and low-contrast secondary text
avoid.why: they disappear entirely in the lighting these devices actually live in

avoid.what: pastels
avoid.why: they wash out under warehouse sodium and outdoor sun alike

style.tradition: flat, utilitarian, near-zero ornament, oversized targets
style.why: every design decision here is subordinate to being operable with gloves on, in a hurry, in bad light

notThis.what: glassmorphism or any translucency, which collapses in direct sunlight
hover-dependent affordances, because there is no hover on a handheld

logistics.density: low on the handheld, very high on the dispatcher's desk
logistics.typography: large, high weight, tabular numerals for consignment and unit counts. Reference numbers grouped so they can be read aloud over radio
logistics.tone: imperative and short. 'Scan the pallet label' beats 'Please scan the pallet label to continue'
forbidden: control targets sized for an office pointer on a device used with gloves
a tracking state with no timestamp
a custody transfer with no named receiving actor

realestate.label: Property, real estate and rental

stakeholders.wants: to judge a place without visiting
stakeholders.fears: discovering a material fact after committing
stakeholders.designImplication: material facts, from tenure to service charge to flood risk, sit with the price and not in a downloadable pack

stakeholders.wants: to list fast and qualify leads
stakeholders.fears: a listing that misrepresents and comes back on them
stakeholders.designImplication: a listing form that permits omission of a material fact is a liability, so required fields here are a legal decision

stakeholders.wants: occupancy and compliance
stakeholders.fears: a certificate that expired
stakeholders.designImplication: compliance certificates are dated objects with expiry states

stakeholders.wants: repairs done and a record of asking
stakeholders.fears: a request with no trail
stakeholders.designImplication: the repair request is an audited thread, visible to both sides identically

stakeholders.wants: accurate advertising and deposit protection
stakeholders.fears: a misdescription
stakeholders.designImplication: advertised measurements and images carry provenance and date

standards: not applicable universally. Where a national property data standard exists it governs listing fields
realestate.regulator: property or estate agency regulator, plus advertising standards

colour.leads: warm neutrals and muted greens or navies, letting photography carry the colour
colour.why: the product is photography. A saturated interface competes with the only thing the user came to look at

avoid.what: strong branded colour adjacent to property imagery
avoid.why: it shifts the perceived colour of the room in the photo, which is a misrepresentation risk

colour.reservedNote: no hue is load-bearing in this sector, so the palette is a brand decision rather than an inherited constraint

style.tradition: editorial with generous imagery, restrained interface chrome
style.why: the sector sells aspiration through photography and reassurance through detail. Both need the interface to get out of the way

notThis.what: dense card grids that crop photography to a square, which hides room proportion

realestate.density: low on the listing, high on the agent's pipeline and the landlord's compliance register
realestate.typography: price and floor area use tabular numerals. Measurements always carry units, and both metric and local convention where the market expects it
realestate.tone: descriptive, never superlative. Advertising standards bind the copy here
forbidden: a material fact available only in a downloadable document
photography with no capture date
an area figure with no stated measurement basis

travel.label: Travel, transport and mobility

stakeholders.wants: to get there, and to know immediately when that changes
stakeholders.fears: a disruption they learn about at the gate
stakeholders.designImplication: the disruption state is a designed screen with rebooking on it, not a red banner

stakeholders.wants: to process a queue
stakeholders.fears: a passenger record that disagrees with the system
stakeholders.designImplication: staff screens show the same record the passenger sees, with the same wording

stakeholders.wants: to reallocate capacity
stakeholders.fears: a cascade nobody modelled
stakeholders.designImplication: knock-on effects are shown, not left to be inferred

stakeholders.wants: assistance that is actually booked
stakeholders.fears: arriving to find no record of it
stakeholders.designImplication: assistance is a booking object with a confirmation, not a checkbox

stakeholders.wants: passenger rights honoured
stakeholders.fears: compensation entitlement not disclosed
stakeholders.designImplication: entitlement appears in the disruption flow, at the moment it arises

standards: IATA NDC for airline content and ordering
GTFS for public transit schedules and real-time
travel.regulator: civil aviation or national transport authority

colour.leads: a confident brand hue with a strictly reserved disruption channel in amber and red
colour.why: the product's hardest moment is disruption, and the palette must have kept a channel free for it

avoid.what: amber or red used for promotion
avoid.why: it is the exact colour the user must trust to mean 'your journey changed'

style.tradition: flat and wayfinding-derived, drawing on transit signage conventions
style.why: the sector has a century of signage practice behind it, and travellers already read it

notThis.what: ornament on time-critical screens, which are read while walking

travel.density: low while travelling, high in operations and in the booking comparison
travel.typography: times and gate or platform identifiers are the largest runs on the screen. Tabular numerals for times and durations, and the 24-hour convention where the market uses it
travel.tone: calm and factual under disruption. State the new fact and the next action in that order
forbidden: a fare quoted without mandatory taxes and charges
a disruption notice with no next action
an assistance request with no confirmation object

media.label: Media, publishing and entertainment

stakeholders.wants: the thing, without obstruction
stakeholders.fears: paying and still being interrupted
stakeholders.designImplication: the paid state must visibly differ from the free one, or the payment feels unhonoured

stakeholders.wants: to shape what leads
stakeholders.fears: an automated feed burying the thing that matters
stakeholders.designImplication: editorial override is a first-class control, not a database edit

stakeholders.wants: their work presented as they built it
stakeholders.fears: a layout that breaks a long-form piece
stakeholders.designImplication: long-form templates are a design deliverable, tested at real length

stakeholders.wants: viewable placement
stakeholders.fears: placement next to unsuitable content
stakeholders.designImplication: ad slots are designed into the layout with declared adjacency rules, not injected

stakeholders.wants: clear separation of editorial and paid
stakeholders.fears: advertorial indistinguishable from editorial
stakeholders.designImplication: sponsored labelling is a component with a minimum specification

standards: not applicable for exchange. RSS and schema.org article markup are conventional; broadcast subtitling standards bind where video is served
media.regulator: press or broadcast regulator, plus advertising standards

colour.leads: a restrained editorial base, usually near-monochrome, with one signature accent
colour.why: the content supplies the colour. A publication that colours its own chrome competes with its photography and its illustration

avoid.what: a palette that changes per section
avoid.why: it dissolves the masthead, which is the only thing distinguishing this publication from any other

colour.reservedNote: no hue is load-bearing in this sector, so the palette is a brand decision rather than an inherited constraint

style.tradition: editorial, unambiguously. This is the tradition's home sector
style.why: typographic hierarchy, measure, and grid are what make long-form readable, and long-form is the product

notThis.what: card grids that give every story the same weight, which is the abdication of editing

media.density: low in the reading experience, high in the newsroom or content management surface
media.typography: the central decision of the whole product. Measure capped for sustained reading, a real typographic scale, and a distinct voice between headline and body
media.tone: the publication's own. This is the one sector where house voice outranks any convention here
forbidden: sponsored content not labelled to the regulator's minimum
an interstitial between a paying reader and the content they paid for
autoplay with sound

manufacturing.label: Manufacturing, industrial and plant operations

stakeholders.wants: to know the line is right and stop it if not
stakeholders.fears: a stop they caused and cannot explain
stakeholders.designImplication: the stop control is the largest, most reachable thing on the screen, and it is never adjacent to anything destructive

stakeholders.wants: throughput, downtime and the reason for both
stakeholders.fears: an unattributed stoppage
stakeholders.designImplication: a downtime event requires a reason code at the moment it ends, not at end of shift

stakeholders.wants: the fault history of this asset
stakeholders.fears: replacing a part that was not the cause
stakeholders.designImplication: asset history is a first-class screen keyed to a physical tag

stakeholders.wants: to record a result against a batch
stakeholders.fears: a result recorded against the wrong batch
stakeholders.designImplication: batch identity is confirmed by scan, never typed

stakeholders.wants: traceability from finished unit back to inputs
stakeholders.fears: a recall that cannot be bounded
stakeholders.designImplication: genealogy is a designed capability, not a report someone writes later

standards: OPC UA for machine data
ISA-95 for the enterprise-to-control integration model
GS1 for unit and batch identifiers
manufacturing.regulator: occupational safety authority, plus sector-specific product safety bodies

colour.leads: industrial signalling conventions: red for stop and fault, amber for warning and degraded, green for running
colour.why: this triad is not a design choice. It is inherited from physical plant signage and from ISO safety colours, and operators read it before they read language

avoid.what: green, amber or red for anything other than machine state
avoid.why: an operator glancing at a screen from four metres reads only colour, and any other use of those three hues is a safety defect

avoid.what: low-contrast interfaces
avoid.why: these screens are behind polycarbonate, in dust, under high ambient light

style.tradition: flat, utilitarian, oversized, high contrast
style.why: read at distance, operated with gloves, often through a protective panel

notThis.what: any ornament, animation or translucency on a control surface

manufacturing.density: medium on the line, high in the supervisor and quality surfaces
manufacturing.typography: very large for state and counts, tabular numerals throughout, unit always adjacent to the number
manufacturing.tone: imperative and unambiguous. No hedging on a machine state
forbidden: a stop control that can be reached accidentally, or that requires a confirmation
using the safety colour triad decoratively
a quality result recorded against a typed batch number

energy.label: Energy, utilities and metering

stakeholders.wants: to understand a bill and reduce it
stakeholders.fears: an estimated bill that turns out to be wrong
stakeholders.designImplication: an estimated reading is labelled as estimated everywhere it appears, including in the total

stakeholders.wants: the job, the asset and the safety notes
stakeholders.fears: arriving at an asset that is not what the record says
stakeholders.designImplication: asset records carry a last-verified date, outdoors, offline

stakeholders.wants: load and fault location
stakeholders.fears: a fault they localise wrongly
stakeholders.designImplication: confidence in a fault location is shown, not hidden behind a single pin

stakeholders.wants: readings that reconcile
stakeholders.fears: a tariff change applied to the wrong period
stakeholders.designImplication: tariff periods are visible objects with boundaries

stakeholders.wants: tariff transparency and vulnerable-customer protection
stakeholders.fears: a disconnection path with no safeguard
stakeholders.designImplication: any flow that can end supply carries a mandated safeguard step

standards: IEC 61968 and 61970 for utility data exchange
DLMS/COSEM for smart meter communication

colour.leads: a calm base with a consumption scale that is not itself a judgement
colour.why: a consumption chart coloured red at the high end tells a customer they are bad, which is a claim the product cannot support without knowing their circumstances

avoid.what: red for high consumption
avoid.why: it moralises a number that may reflect a medical need, a cold house, or a larger family

avoid.what: green as a reward for low usage
avoid.why: the same problem in reverse, and it is the one that draws complaints

reserved.for: a safety or supply fault, never high consumption

style.tradition: flat and data-forward for the customer, utilitarian for the field
style.why: the customer product is a chart and a bill; the field product is a rugged offline tool. Two styles, declared separately

notThis.what: gamified treatments of consumption, which fail badly for customers in fuel poverty

energy.density: medium for the customer, high for control room, low for field
energy.typography: tabular numerals for readings and amounts. Units always present, and a reading never rendered without its date and its estimated-or-actual flag
energy.tone: factual and non-judgemental about consumption. Directive about safety
forbidden: an estimated reading presented as actual
colouring consumption as good or bad
a disconnection flow with no vulnerability check

government.label: Government and public sector services

stakeholders.wants: to complete an obligation and be done
stakeholders.fears: a form they get wrong and a consequence they cannot appeal
stakeholders.designImplication: the audience is everyone, which means the lowest assumed literacy, the oldest device, and the worst connection are the design targets, not edge cases

stakeholders.wants: to decide consistently
stakeholders.fears: a decision they cannot justify on review
stakeholders.designImplication: the evidence behind a decision is on the decision screen

stakeholders.wants: the rule implemented as written
stakeholders.fears: an interface that quietly changes eligibility
stakeholders.designImplication: eligibility logic is surfaced in language, not only in code

stakeholders.wants: to act for someone else
stakeholders.fears: a system with no concept of assisted digital
stakeholders.designImplication: acting on behalf of another person is a designed role, not a shared password

stakeholders.wants: equal treatment demonstrated
stakeholders.fears: a service that excludes a group
stakeholders.designImplication: accessibility conformance is a statutory floor here, commonly WCAG 2.2 AA, and it is auditable

standards: not applicable for exchange in most services. National design systems, such as the UK GOV.UK Design System or US Web Design System, are often mandatory rather than advisory
government.regulator: the sponsoring department, plus a statutory accessibility and equalities regime

colour.leads: whatever the mandated national design system specifies, and if none is mandated, a high-contrast restrained palette with a single action colour
colour.why: in this sector a house style is frequently a legal instrument. Check for a mandated system before proposing anything, because proposing a palette against one is proposing non-compliance

avoid.what: a bespoke palette where a national design system applies
avoid.why: it is not a taste disagreement, it is a compliance failure

avoid.what: contrast ratios at the minimum
avoid.why: the statutory floor is a floor, and this audience includes every vision profile in the population

colour.reservedNote: no hue is load-bearing in this sector, so the palette is a brand decision rather than an inherited constraint

style.tradition: flat, plain, typographic, near-zero ornament, in the lineage of GOV.UK
style.why: the sector proved empirically that plainness raises completion rates for services people are obliged to use and do not enjoy

notThis.what: marketing styling on a statutory service, which reads as an attempt to persuade someone who has no choice

government.density: low for the citizen, deliberately: one thing per page is the sector's established pattern and it outperforms grouped forms
government.typography: large body text, generous line height, and a reading age target well below the national average. Plain-language testing is part of the deliverable
government.tone: plain, direct, second person. Say what happens next and by when
forbidden: a service with no non-digital route
accessibility below the statutory conformance level
eligibility rules a citizen cannot read in language
a bespoke component where a mandated design system provides one

nonprofit.label: Charity, non-profit and fundraising

stakeholders.wants: to give easily and know it landed somewhere real
stakeholders.fears: that most of it goes on overheads
stakeholders.designImplication: the donation flow is the shortest path in the product, and impact is stated with a source

stakeholders.wants: help without humiliation
stakeholders.fears: being made into a case study
stakeholders.designImplication: beneficiary imagery and stories require consent, and the design must carry that as a field. This is the sector's central ethical failure mode

stakeholders.wants: a shift and what to bring
stakeholders.fears: turning up to the wrong thing
stakeholders.designImplication: volunteer-facing screens are as considered as donor-facing ones, which is rarely true in practice

stakeholders.wants: restricted and unrestricted funds separated
stakeholders.fears: restricted funds spent outside their restriction
stakeholders.designImplication: fund restriction is a data concept that must appear in the interface

stakeholders.wants: honest fundraising and safeguarding
stakeholders.fears: pressure tactics on vulnerable donors
stakeholders.designImplication: no urgency device that a regulator would read as pressure

standards: not applicable. Gift Aid or equivalent tax-relief schemes impose their own declaration requirements where they exist
nonprofit.regulator: charity commission or equivalent, plus fundraising standards bodies

colour.leads: a warm, human palette, usually a single strong brand hue with generous neutral
colour.why: the sector runs on identification with a cause. Corporate restraint reads as distance

avoid.what: distress-signalling colour combined with urgency copy
avoid.why: together they constitute the pressure pattern fundraising regulators act on

colour.reservedNote: no hue is load-bearing in this sector, so the palette is a brand decision rather than an inherited constraint

style.tradition: editorial and photographic, warm, human
style.why: the product is a story that asks for something. Photography and typographic voice carry it

notThis.what: dashboard styling on a donation page

nonprofit.density: low throughout the donor and volunteer surfaces, higher in fund administration
nonprofit.typography: readable at length, because the case for support is long-form. Amounts in tabular numerals
nonprofit.tone: honest and specific. A named, sourced outcome beats an emotional superlative, and it converts better
forbidden: beneficiary imagery without recorded consent
a recurring-gift default the donor did not choose
an unsubstantiated impact claim
urgency devices that are not true

hr.label: Human resources, recruitment and people operations

stakeholders.wants: to apply without re-typing their life and to hear back
stakeholders.fears: silence, and a filter they cannot see
stakeholders.designImplication: the candidate is the least-served user in this sector's products, and rejection is a designed state with a real message

stakeholders.wants: to compare fairly and quickly
stakeholders.fears: a hire that was a mistake
stakeholders.designImplication: structured comparison surfaces, not free-text impressions

stakeholders.wants: pipeline throughput
stakeholders.fears: a candidate lost between stages
stakeholders.designImplication: stage age is visible on every candidate

stakeholders.wants: leave, pay and personal data without asking a person
stakeholders.fears: their manager seeing something private
stakeholders.designImplication: the visibility boundary between employee, manager and HR is a design surface, and getting it wrong is the sector's classic incident

stakeholders.wants: non-discrimination and lawful processing
stakeholders.fears: automated decisions with no human review
stakeholders.designImplication: any automated ranking or filter is disclosed, explainable, and has a human review path

standards: not applicable for exchange. Payroll interfaces are set nationally by the tax authority
hr.regulator: employment authority and data protection regulator, plus works councils where they exist

colour.leads: a professional but warm palette, typically a confident blue, green or purple with human neutrals
colour.why: the product sits between an institution and a person, and it must not read as purely institutional to the person

avoid.what: red for a rejected or unsuccessful state
avoid.why: the person reading it is being told no about their livelihood, and a red badge adds nothing but sting

colour.reservedNote: no hue is load-bearing in this sector, so the palette is a brand decision rather than an inherited constraint

style.tradition: flat, clean, professional, with restrained warmth
style.why: it is workplace software that people use on some of the worst days of their working life

notThis.what: celebratory or gamified treatments around performance and compensation

hr.density: high in the recruiter's pipeline and the HR admin, low in every candidate and employee surface
hr.typography: unremarkable and legible. Salary and leave balances in tabular numerals
hr.tone: human and clear. A rejection says a real thing; a leave balance says exactly what is left and when it expires
forbidden: an automated filter with no disclosure and no human review path
a candidate outcome that is silence
manager visibility of an employee's protected or medical data
collecting protected characteristics without a stated lawful purpose

agriculture.label: Agriculture, farming and agritech

stakeholders.wants: a decision for this field, this week
stakeholders.fears: acting on data that was not from their land
stakeholders.designImplication: outdoors, in sun, with gloves, on a phone with poor signal. Offline capability is a design requirement, not a nice-to-have

stakeholders.wants: trial and treatment history per parcel
stakeholders.fears: a recommendation that breaks a residue rule
stakeholders.designImplication: withholding periods and application limits are hard constraints in the interface

stakeholders.wants: the task and where
stakeholders.fears: a map they cannot read in a cab
stakeholders.designImplication: very large targets, high contrast, one-handed, glanceable from a moving vehicle

stakeholders.wants: traceability and assurance status
stakeholders.fears: a consignment that fails assurance at intake
stakeholders.designImplication: assurance status is a visible state on a batch

stakeholders.wants: input records and subsidy compliance
stakeholders.fears: a treatment applied inside a withholding period
stakeholders.designImplication: treatment records carry dates that the system can enforce against

standards: not applicable universally. ISOBUS for machinery interoperability, and national farm-assurance schemes govern record-keeping
agriculture.regulator: agriculture or rural payments authority, plus food safety

colour.leads: earth and crop greens with high-contrast utility accents
colour.why: the sector's own colour language, and it survives being viewed on a cracked phone in a field

avoid.what: green as a status colour in a product whose base palette is green
avoid.why: the status disappears into the brand

avoid.what: low-contrast anything
avoid.why: direct sunlight is the normal operating condition

colour.reservedNote: no hue is load-bearing in this sector, so the palette is a brand decision rather than an inherited constraint

style.tradition: flat, rugged, oversized, map-forward
style.why: the primary object is a parcel of land, so cartography is the central design problem

notThis.what: dense desktop dashboards as the primary surface, when the primary device is a phone in a tractor cab

agriculture.density: low in the field, high in the office planning surface
agriculture.typography: large, high-weight, tabular numerals for areas, rates and yields. Units always adjacent
agriculture.tone: practical and specific to the parcel. Generic advice is worthless here
forbidden: a treatment recommendation that ignores a withholding period
a product that is unusable offline
data attributed to a field it did not come from

construction.label: Construction, engineering and the built environment

stakeholders.wants: today's task and the current drawing
stakeholders.fears: building from a superseded revision
stakeholders.designImplication: drawing revision is the most prominent thing on any drawing screen. This is the sector's costliest recurring failure

stakeholders.wants: progress, and the blockers
stakeholders.fears: a safety incident on their site
stakeholders.designImplication: safety observations are a one-tap capture from anywhere in the product

stakeholders.wants: their intent built as specified
stakeholders.fears: a substitution nobody told them about
stakeholders.designImplication: a change request is an audited object with a named approver

stakeholders.wants: measured progress tied to valuation
stakeholders.fears: paying for work not done
stakeholders.designImplication: progress claims reference evidence, and the evidence is dated and located

stakeholders.wants: a golden thread of information
stakeholders.fears: a building whose as-built record does not exist
stakeholders.designImplication: the record of what was actually built is a product output, not a byproduct

standards: IFC for building information exchange
ISO 19650 for information management across the asset lifecycle
construction.regulator: building safety and occupational safety authorities

colour.leads: high-visibility utility palette echoing site signage, with a hard-reserved safety channel
colour.why: site users already read hi-vis and hazard conventions, and the screen should not contradict the hoarding

avoid.what: hazard yellow and black for non-safety UI
avoid.why: on a construction site that pairing means hazard, and it means it before anyone reads a word

avoid.what: low contrast
avoid.why: outdoors, dusty screen, gloved hands, bright sky

style.tradition: flat, rugged, document-and-drawing-forward
style.why: the artefacts are drawings and records, and the environment is hostile to anything delicate

notThis.what: thin weights and light greys, which are unreadable in the actual operating conditions

construction.density: low on site, high in the office coordination surface
construction.typography: large and heavy. Revision codes and drawing numbers never truncate and never wrap
construction.tone: instructional and unambiguous. Safety copy is never softened
forbidden: a drawing shown without its revision
a superseded revision reachable without a warning
a safety observation flow that takes more than one tap to start

fitness.label: Fitness, wellness and consumer health

stakeholders.wants: to keep going
stakeholders.fears: being made to feel like a failure by their own app
stakeholders.designImplication: a broken streak is the sector's most damaging designed moment. Design the recovery, not the loss

stakeholders.wants: to programme and see adherence
stakeholders.fears: prescribing into an injury
stakeholders.designImplication: the coach surface is dense and structured; the member surface is not

stakeholders.wants: class occupancy and retention
stakeholders.fears: no-shows blocking a full class
stakeholders.designImplication: booking and cancellation states are the commercial heart of the product

stakeholders.role: clinician, where health data is involved
stakeholders.wants: data they can trust
stakeholders.fears: a consumer metric presented as clinical
stakeholders.designImplication: consumer sensor data is labelled as such wherever it approaches a clinical reading

stakeholders.wants: health and body claims that can be substantiated
stakeholders.fears: an outcome claim with no evidence
stakeholders.designImplication: outcome claims carry substantiation, and body-composition claims are the most scrutinised

standards: not applicable. Where the product touches clinical data, the healthcare standards apply instead and the product changes category
fitness.regulator: advertising standards, plus the health regulator once claims become medical

colour.leads: energetic but not aggressive: a confident accent over calm neutrals, frequently with a dark mode as the primary
colour.why: much of this product's use is early morning, late evening, and in a dim gym, so dark is often the default rather than the alternative

avoid.what: red for a missed day or a broken streak
avoid.why: it punishes the user for the exact behaviour the product exists to rebuild

avoid.what: clinical blues and whites
avoid.why: they position a wellness product as a medical one, which is a regulatory claim as well as a tonal one

colour.reservedNote: no hue is load-bearing in this sector, so the palette is a brand decision rather than an inherited constraint

style.tradition: flat with bold typographic treatment, dark-first, imagery-supported
style.why: the product is read at a glance mid-activity, and legibility under motion outranks nuance

notThis.what: dense data-dashboard styling for a consumer, which is the most common overreach in this sector

fitness.density: low for the member, high for the coach
fitness.typography: large numerals for the current metric, tabular where series are compared. The number being tracked is the largest thing on the screen
fitness.tone: supportive and non-judgemental. Never shame a lapse, and never imply a body outcome
forbidden: a body-composition or weight-loss claim with no substantiation
presenting consumer sensor data as a clinical measurement
punitive framing of a missed day
default-public sharing of health or location data

telecom.label: Telecommunications and connectivity

stakeholders.wants: to know what they are using and what it costs
stakeholders.fears: a bill shock from something they did not know was chargeable
stakeholders.designImplication: usage against allowance is the primary screen, and any chargeable action outside the allowance is confirmed before it happens

stakeholders.wants: line state and history
stakeholders.fears: telling a customer something the network contradicts
stakeholders.designImplication: the agent and the customer see the same diagnostic result, worded the same way

stakeholders.wants: incident scope and restoration time
stakeholders.fears: an outage customers learn about from social media first
stakeholders.designImplication: the outage state is a designed, proactive screen with an estimate on it

stakeholders.wants: to provision without escalating
stakeholders.fears: an activation that half-completes
stakeholders.designImplication: provisioning is a state machine with every intermediate state designed

stakeholders.wants: contract transparency and switching that works
stakeholders.fears: a barrier to leaving
stakeholders.designImplication: contract end date, exit terms and the switching code are reachable in one step

standards: not applicable at the interface. Number portability and switching processes are mandated nationally by the regulator

colour.leads: a strong single brand hue, this being one of the most brand-driven sectors, over neutral chrome
colour.why: telco brands are built on colour recognition, and the interface is a brand surface. What is not negotiable is that service state keeps its own channel

avoid.what: the brand hue used for service state
avoid.why: if the brand is red, an outage cannot be red

reserved.for: outage and degradation, kept clear of the brand hue

style.tradition: flat and consumer-friendly on self-serve, utilitarian in operations
style.why: self-serve exists to deflect calls, so it must be legible to everyone the network serves, which is everyone

notThis.what: ornament between the customer and their usage figure

telecom.density: low on self-serve, high in operations and support tooling
telecom.typography: usage figures and allowances in tabular numerals with the unit adjacent. Contract dates never abbreviated ambiguously
telecom.tone: plain about cost, honest about outages. An estimate is better than silence and worse than a wrong promise
forbidden: a chargeable action outside the allowance with no confirmation
an outage the product does not acknowledge
a switching or cancellation path that is longer than the sign-up path
speed or coverage claims without the regulator's required qualification

professional.label: Professional services: agency, studio, consultancy and personal practice

stakeholders.wants: to know whether this person or firm has done their problem before
stakeholders.fears: hiring someone whose best work was somebody else's
stakeholders.designImplication: every piece of work states what THIS practitioner did on it. A case study with no stated role is the sector's defining failure, and an experienced buyer discounts it entirely

stakeholders.wants: evidence of level, in about forty seconds
stakeholders.fears: a portfolio that looks good and shows no thinking
stakeholders.designImplication: the outcome and the constraint are as prominent as the visual. Screenshots without a problem statement read as decoration

stakeholders.wants: to judge craft
stakeholders.fears: nothing, they are the most forgiving reader
stakeholders.designImplication: the peer audience is the one everyone designs for and the one who does not hire. Design for the buyer instead

stakeholders.wants: work that resembles the work they want next
stakeholders.fears: being typecast by their oldest project
stakeholders.designImplication: the ordering of work is a positioning decision, not a chronology

stakeholders.wants: their material not published
stakeholders.fears: commercially sensitive work made public
stakeholders.designImplication: an NDA state is a real state: work shown in outline, without the artefact, and labelled as such

standards: not applicable: there is no exchange format and no regulator for most practices. Regulated professions such as architecture, accountancy or law inherit their own body's rules on advertising and title use
professional.regulator: advertising standards for claims. A regulated profession also answers to its registration body on how it may describe itself

colour.leads: a restrained near-neutral base with one signature accent, letting the work carry the colour
colour.why: the page's job is to make the work look like the work. A strongly coloured interface changes the perceived colour of every screenshot on it, which is a misrepresentation as much as an aesthetic problem

avoid.what: a saturated background behind work samples
avoid.why: it shifts the apparent hue of the work and makes two projects look like one palette

avoid.what: gradient-heavy treatments borrowed from whatever launched last year
avoid.why: it dates the page to a season, and the page has to hold for two years

colour.reservedNote: no hue is load-bearing in this sector, so the palette is a brand decision rather than an inherited constraint

style.tradition: editorial or minimalism, with typography carrying the craft argument
style.why: in this sector the interface is itself a work sample. The typographic decisions are read as evidence of judgement before a single case study is opened

notThis.what: template-derived layouts that a buyer has seen forty times, which say the practitioner did not make a decision
maximalism, unless maximalism is demonstrably the practice's actual discipline

professional.density: low. The work is the content and it needs air. The one dense surface is a detailed index for a buyer who already wants to compare
professional.typography: the single strongest signal in the whole sector. A real scale, a considered pairing, and correct measure will be read as competence; defaults will be read as its absence. Numbers in outcomes use tabular figures so results align
professional.tone: specific and evidenced. 'Rebuilt checkout, cart abandonment fell 18 percent over two quarters' beats every adjective. Never 'passionate about'
forbidden: a case study that does not state what this practitioner personally did
an outcome claim with no number or no timeframe
client work shown without permission where confidentiality applies
a contact route that does not work, which is the most common defect in the entire sector

devtools.label: Developer tools, APIs and technical infrastructure

stakeholders.wants: to reach a working call in minutes
stakeholders.fears: a product whose docs hide whether it does the thing
stakeholders.designImplication: time to first successful call is the product's primary metric, and the landing page's job is to shorten it. This audience reads code before prose

stakeholders.wants: an error message that names the fix
stakeholders.fears: a failure mode the docs do not cover
stakeholders.designImplication: error copy is product surface here, not an afterthought. It is read more often than the marketing site

stakeholders.wants: pricing, limits and an exit path
stakeholders.fears: a dependency they cannot leave
stakeholders.designImplication: rate limits, pricing tiers and data export are first-class pages, not footer links

stakeholders.wants: status, incidents and versioning honesty
stakeholders.fears: a breaking change in a minor version
stakeholders.designImplication: a public status page and a real deprecation policy are product features

stakeholders.wants: auth model, data handling and compliance posture
stakeholders.fears: secrets in an example
stakeholders.designImplication: no code sample anywhere contains a plausible-looking real credential

standards: OpenAPI for HTTP interface description
Semantic Versioning for release contracts
OAuth 2.0 and OIDC where third-party auth is involved
devtools.regulator: none for the interface. Data protection law applies to whatever the product processes

colour.leads: dark-first, with a restrained accent and syntax colouring that survives both themes
colour.why: this audience works in a dark editor all day and switches to the docs in the same glance. A light-only product is read as unserious by a measurable share of the audience

avoid.what: a syntax palette that fails contrast in one of the two themes
avoid.why: code samples are the primary content, and half the audience reads them in the other theme

avoid.what: marketing gradients over code blocks
avoid.why: they reduce the legibility of the one thing the visitor came for

colour.reservedNote: no hue is load-bearing in this sector, so the palette is a brand decision rather than an inherited constraint

style.tradition: flat, typographic, docs-forward, with the terminal as an acknowledged visual ancestor
style.why: credibility in this sector comes from showing the actual interface early, and the actual interface is text

notThis.what: illustration-led marketing pages that delay the first code sample
skeuomorphism, which reads as a decade out of date to this audience specifically

devtools.density: high. This audience prefers a dense reference to a friendly walkthrough, and resents pagination in documentation
devtools.typography: a real monospace pairing is mandatory, and code is never rendered in a proportional face. Line numbers and diffs need tabular alignment. Copy buttons on every sample
devtools.tone: terse, technical, honest about limits. State the rate limit and the failure mode. This audience punishes marketing language harder than any other
forbidden: a code sample that does not run as written
a real or realistic credential in an example
a breaking change shipped in a non-major version
documentation that lags the shipped version with no version selector

gaming.label: Games and interactive entertainment

stakeholders.wants: to get into the game
stakeholders.fears: a menu between them and playing
stakeholders.designImplication: every screen outside gameplay is friction the player is tolerating. Path length to play is the design's primary constraint

stakeholders.wants: to know exactly what they are buying
stakeholders.fears: a currency conversion designed to obscure real cost
stakeholders.designImplication: virtual currency that hides real money cost is regulated in a growing number of markets and is a design decision with legal weight

stakeholders.wants: spend controls that work
stakeholders.fears: an unexpected charge
stakeholders.designImplication: spend limits and purchase confirmation are product features, and in several markets they are mandatory

stakeholders.wants: tools to act fast
stakeholders.fears: harassment they cannot action
stakeholders.designImplication: reporting and blocking are first-class flows, reachable from wherever the harm happens

stakeholders.role: platform holder and age ratings body
stakeholders.wants: compliance with store and rating rules
stakeholders.fears: content or monetisation outside the rating
stakeholders.designImplication: the platform's own interface guidelines outrank house style, and store rejection is the enforcement

standards: platform certification requirements from each console or app store
PEGI, ESRB or the local equivalent for age rating
gaming.regulator: age ratings body, plus consumer and gambling regulators where loot mechanics are involved

colour.leads: whatever the game's own art direction dictates, with an interface palette derived from it rather than imposed on it
colour.why: this is the one sector where the interface serves an existing visual world. A generic product palette breaks the fiction the game spent its budget building

avoid.what: interface colour that competes with gameplay legibility
avoid.why: a health bar that is hard to read is a defect, not a style

avoid.what: colour as the only channel for team, faction or status
avoid.why: competitive play at speed plus colour vision deficiency is a fairness problem

reserved.for: identity, and never the only channel for it

style.tradition: diegetic or art-directed, extending the game's own world into its menus
style.why: the interface is part of the fiction, and the sector's best work makes it feel like an artefact from inside the game

notThis.what: default flat product styling, which reads as placeholder art
an interface that ignores the game's own typography and palette

gaming.density: low in-game, higher in inventory, progression and store surfaces
gaming.typography: legible at distance on a television and at arm's length on a handheld, which is a harder constraint than it looks. Numerals tabular wherever stats compare
gaming.tone: in the game's voice, always. Except for purchase, safety and age-gating copy, which is plain and outside the fiction
forbidden: obscuring the real-money cost of a purchase behind a currency conversion
a loot mechanic with undisclosed odds where disclosure is required
a reporting flow that is harder to reach than the harm
gameplay-critical information conveyed by colour alone

automotive.label: Automotive: retail, service, fleet and in-vehicle

stakeholders.wants: the real total cost including finance
stakeholders.fears: a monthly figure that hides the term and the balloon
stakeholders.designImplication: finance illustrations carry APR, term and total payable with equal prominence to the monthly figure, and in most markets that is a legal requirement

stakeholders.wants: to act without looking away from the road
stakeholders.fears: a distraction that causes an incident
stakeholders.designImplication: in-vehicle surfaces are governed by driver-distraction guidelines with real limits on interaction depth and glance time. This is a safety constraint, not a usability one

stakeholders.wants: an authorisation the customer understood
stakeholders.fears: a bill disputed at collection
stakeholders.designImplication: work authorisation is an evidenced, timestamped agreement with the items itemised

stakeholders.wants: utilisation, cost per mile and compliance
stakeholders.fears: a vehicle out of test or insurance
stakeholders.designImplication: expiry dates are states with warning thresholds, not fields

stakeholders.wants: recall reach and distraction compliance
stakeholders.fears: a recall notice nobody saw
stakeholders.designImplication: a safety recall is a designed interruption, not a notification among others

standards: ISO 15118 for EV charging communication
OCPP for charge point management
NHTSA or equivalent driver-distraction guidelines for in-vehicle interfaces
automotive.regulator: vehicle safety authority, plus consumer credit regulation on finance

colour.leads: a restrained automotive palette letting vehicle imagery lead, with a hard-reserved warning channel for vehicle state
colour.why: the vehicle telltale conventions are internationally standardised, and a product that borrows amber or red for anything else contradicts the dashboard the driver is already reading

avoid.what: amber or red for anything but vehicle or safety state
avoid.why: they mean something specific on every dashboard in the world

avoid.what: a coloured background behind vehicle photography
avoid.why: paint colour is a purchase decision and the interface must not tint it

style.tradition: editorial and photographic in retail, flat and oversized in-vehicle
style.why: retail sells with imagery; the in-vehicle surface is read in under two seconds at a time

notThis.what: dense information architecture on any in-vehicle surface, which is a documented safety failure
low-contrast styling anywhere the sun reaches, which in a car is everywhere

automotive.density: medium in retail, very low in-vehicle, high in fleet and service management
automotive.typography: large and high contrast in-vehicle. Prices, ranges and finance figures in tabular numerals, with units always present
automotive.tone: factual on cost and range. Range estimates carry their conditions, because a range figure without conditions is the sector's most complained-about claim
forbidden: a monthly finance figure without APR, term and total payable
an in-vehicle interaction requiring more glances than the distraction guideline allows
a range or efficiency claim with no stated test condition
a safety recall delivered as an ordinary notification

events.label: Events, ticketing and venues

stakeholders.wants: a ticket that will scan and a seat they understood
stakeholders.fears: arriving with a ticket that does not work
stakeholders.designImplication: the ticket must work offline, at a gate, on a dying phone, in bright sun. That single constraint drives most of the design

stakeholders.wants: to sell out and to control the on-sale
stakeholders.fears: a queue that collapses at on-sale
stakeholders.designImplication: the queue and the sold-out states are primary designed screens, because they are what most buyers will actually see

stakeholders.wants: to scan fast in a crowd
stakeholders.fears: a scan that is ambiguous
stakeholders.designImplication: scan feedback is unmistakable at a metre, in noise, in the dark

stakeholders.wants: a seat that meets their needs, bookable directly
stakeholders.fears: a phone-only path that is closed when they need it
stakeholders.designImplication: accessible seating is bookable in the same flow as any other seat. Routing it to a phone line is the sector's standing failure

stakeholders.wants: the full price shown up front and resale rules honoured
stakeholders.fears: fees revealed at the final step
stakeholders.designImplication: all-in pricing at first display is now mandated in a growing number of markets

standards: not applicable for exchange. Barcode and NFC ticket formats are set by the scanning infrastructure in use
events.regulator: consumer protection authority, plus local licensing for the venue

colour.leads: the event's or artist's own identity, over a neutral transactional chrome
colour.why: people buy the event, not the platform, and the platform's colour should not compete with the poster

avoid.what: urgency red used both for scarcity and for errors
avoid.why: they collide at the checkout, which is the exact moment both appear

colour.reservedNote: no hue is load-bearing in this sector, so the palette is a brand decision rather than an inherited constraint

style.tradition: editorial and poster-derived for discovery, utilitarian for checkout and the ticket itself
style.why: discovery is culture and checkout is infrastructure. Styling them the same makes one of them fail

notThis.what: decorative treatments on the ticket surface, which must survive a low-brightness screen and a scratched protector

events.density: low in discovery, high in the seat map, minimal on the ticket
events.typography: date, time, door and seat are the largest runs on the ticket, and they never truncate. Times carry the timezone where an event can be booked from elsewhere
events.tone: clear about what is included and what it costs in total. Factual under queue and sold-out states
forbidden: fees revealed only at the final step
a ticket that requires connectivity to display
accessible seating that cannot be booked in the normal flow
a scarcity claim that is not true

beauty.label: Beauty, salon, spa and personal care services

stakeholders.wants: the right person, at a time that works, at a price they knew
stakeholders.fears: a result that is not what they asked for
stakeholders.designImplication: reference imagery is part of the booking, because the gap between described and expected outcome is this sector's whole risk

stakeholders.wants: a column that reflects real service durations
stakeholders.fears: a booking that does not leave enough time
stakeholders.designImplication: service duration varies by practitioner and by client history, so a fixed-duration booking model will be wrong

stakeholders.wants: utilisation and reduced no-shows
stakeholders.fears: a deposit policy that loses clients
stakeholders.designImplication: the deposit and cancellation policy is shown before booking, not in terms

stakeholders.role: client with allergies or a skin condition
stakeholders.wants: a patch test recorded
stakeholders.fears: a reaction to a product nobody checked
stakeholders.designImplication: patch test status is a booking precondition for the services that require it, and it expires

stakeholders.role: local health or trading standards authority
stakeholders.wants: hygiene and cosmetic claims within the law
stakeholders.fears: a treatment claim that is medical
stakeholders.designImplication: a cosmetic product may not claim a medical effect, and the copy is where that line is crossed

standards: not applicable. Cosmetic product claims are governed by national cosmetics regulation, and aesthetic treatments may fall under medical regulation
beauty.regulator: local authority environmental health, plus advertising standards on claims

colour.leads: the salon's own identity, typically warm neutrals, muted earth tones or a single sophisticated accent
colour.why: the sector sells taste, and the interface is read as evidence of the salon's taste before any photograph is

avoid.what: strong interface colour beside before-and-after imagery
avoid.why: it shifts perceived skin tone and hair colour, which is both a trust and a claims problem

avoid.what: clinical white and blue for a non-medical service
avoid.why: it implies a medical claim the business is not licensed to make

colour.reservedNote: no hue is load-bearing in this sector, so the palette is a brand decision rather than an inherited constraint

style.tradition: editorial and photographic, restrained, with generous whitespace
style.why: this is an aspiration purchase and the reference imagery is the product

notThis.what: dense booking-system styling on the client-facing surface, which is what most salon software looks like and why salons dislike it

beauty.density: low for the client, high on the practitioner's day view
beauty.typography: an expressive display face is appropriate and expected here. Prices, durations and policy text stay plain and never fall below 14px
beauty.tone: warm and specific. Precise about duration, price and what the appointment includes
forbidden: a medical claim for a cosmetic treatment
before-and-after imagery that is retouched or not from this practitioner
a deposit or cancellation charge disclosed only after booking
booking a patch-test-required service with no valid patch test

security.label: Cybersecurity, identity and trust operations

stakeholders.wants: to triage the real thing among the noise
stakeholders.fears: alert fatigue burying the one that mattered
stakeholders.designImplication: severity must be honest. A product that marks everything critical has no severity, and this is the sector's endemic design failure

stakeholders.wants: scope, blast radius and containment in one place
stakeholders.fears: acting on a stale picture during an incident
stakeholders.designImplication: every view during an incident carries its own freshness, because a dashboard that silently stopped updating is worse than no dashboard

stakeholders.wants: posture and residual risk they can present
stakeholders.fears: a score that cannot be explained to a board
stakeholders.designImplication: any composite score shows its inputs, or it will not survive its first challenge

stakeholders.wants: to do their job
stakeholders.fears: a control that makes the job impossible
stakeholders.designImplication: friction has a budget. A control that is routinely bypassed is a control that does not exist

stakeholders.wants: evidence that a control operated
stakeholders.fears: a control asserted with no record
stakeholders.designImplication: evidence export is a designed capability

standards: ISO/IEC 27001 for the management system
NIST Cybersecurity Framework for structure
OWASP ASVS for application verification
MITRE ATT&CK for describing technique coverage
security.regulator: sector regulator plus the data protection authority, with breach notification deadlines that are hard limits

colour.leads: dark-first operational palette with a strictly graduated severity scale
colour.why: analysts work in dark rooms for long shifts, and the severity scale is the single most-read encoding in the product

avoid.what: red for anything that is not the top severity
avoid.why: the moment two severities are red, the scale has collapsed to one

avoid.what: severity by colour alone
avoid.why: an analyst on a long shift with any colour vision deficiency is exactly the reader who will miss it

style.tradition: flat, dense, data-forward, in the operations-console lineage
style.why: the work is correlation across many signals, and every pixel of ornament is a pixel not spent on a signal

notThis.what: marketing-styled dashboards that prioritise a big number over the queue
gauge and speedometer metaphors, which occupy area proportional to nothing

security.density: very high. This is the densest category of professional interface, and analysts resent whitespace that costs them a row
security.typography: monospace for hashes, addresses and identifiers, always, so that a transposed character is visible. Timestamps carry timezone and never abbreviate the year
security.tone: precise and calibrated. Never dramatise a finding, and never soften one
forbidden: a severity scale where everything is critical
a dashboard that does not show when it last updated
an identifier or hash rendered in a proportional face
a composite risk score with no visible inputs
